תניא, 73a.8-9 -- the baraita as first cited
תניא נמי הכי, 73a.12-14 -- cited again at 73a.18 (מיתיבי)
the Sages disputing R' Meir on the fetus's limb
73a.10 -- ואמרי לה כדי, some give it unattributed
אלא אי אתמר הכי אתמר (73b.3) -- the corrected report of the amoraic dispute

props.gloss_en: baraita A as cited: R' Meir: who purified this limb from carcass impurity? its mother's slaughter! if so, let it permit it for eating! they said: [slaughter] protects what is not her body more than her body
the Sages: the slaughter of its mother purified this limb [of the fetus] from carcass impurity
the Sages: [slaughter] protects what is not her body more than [it protects] her body
as we learned [in the mishna]: one who cuts from the fetus in her womb -- it is permitted to eat; from the spleen and the kidneys -- forbidden to eat

Rava: the baraita is lacking, and this is what it teaches: R' Meir's 'if so, permit it' is answered by 'let the tereifa prove it', and 'it protects what is not her body more' answers his further reply
the Sages: let the tereifa prove it -- its slaughter purifies it from carcass impurity and does not permit it for eating
baraita B: R' Meir: who purified this limb? they: its mother's slaughter. [he:] if so, permit it for eating! they: let the tereifa prove it...
[R' Meir in baraita B:] the tereifa's slaughter purifies her and the limb hanging from her -- what is her body
Reish Lakish: as the dispute [of R' Meir and the Sages] in fetuses, so is the dispute in [hanging] limbs
R' Yochanan: the dispute is in the limb of a fetus
R' Yochanan (version 1): but in an animal's [hanging] limb all agree that slaughter makes [it] fallen
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina: R' Yochanan's reason for the Sages -- this [fetus's limb] has a remedy by return, and that [hanging limb] has no remedy by return
R' Yochanan (version 2): but in an animal's [hanging] limb all agree that slaughter does not make [it] fallen
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina: R' Yochanan's reason for R' Meir -- this [hanging limb] is her body, and that [fetus's limb] is not her body
R' Yochanan: all agree that death makes [a hanging limb] fallen
R' Yochanan: and slaughter does not make [it] fallen
the dictum is about the limb of a fetus
rather the dictum is about an animal's [hanging] limb
the mishna: if the animal died -- the [hanging] flesh needs hechsher, and the limb imparts impurity as a limb from the living, not as a limb from a carcass; the words of R' Meir
the mishna: if the animal was slaughtered -- they were made susceptible by its blood; the words of R' Meir
R' Shimon: they were not made susceptible [by its blood]
from that [mishna] I would have said: 'they were made susceptible' refers to the flesh [only]
you might say: [the plural is] one for flesh separating from the animal and one for flesh separating from the limb

the baraita: 'and flesh torn in the field you shall not eat' (Ex 22:30) -- to include the limb and the flesh hanging on a domestic animal, a wild animal or a bird, that one slaughtered: they are forbidden
R' Yochanan (via Rabba bar bar Chana): they carry only a mitzva of separation
Rav (via Rav Yehuda): one who ate this [hanging limb] is flogged
Rav (via Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta): one who ate this is not flogged
Rav Yosef: what I said [lashes] is of death, which makes [the limb] fallen
Rav Yosef: what he said [no lashes] is of slaughter, which does not make [it] fallen
Rava: the source of the Sages' 'death makes fallen, slaughter does not' is 'and anything on which any of them falls in their death shall be impure' (Lev 11:32)
[entertained:] 'in their death' excludes [impurity] in their life
Rav Chisda: the dispute is in the limb of a live fetus
Rav Chisda: but in the limb of a dead fetus all agree slaughter makes [it] fallen
Rabba: as the dispute in this [live fetus], so the dispute in that [dead fetus]

schemas.gloss_en: טרפה תוכיח, ששחיטתה מטהרתה מידי נבלה ואינה מתירתה באכילה -- as the tereifa's slaughter purifies it without permitting it, so the mother's slaughter purifies the limb

grounds.gloss_en: R' Meir: לא, אם טיהרה שחיטת טרפה אותה, דבר שהיא גופה, תטהר את האבר דבר שאינו גופה? (baraita B, 73a.13: אותה ואת האבר המדולדל בה... תטהר את העובר)

answered_by.gloss_en: הרבה מצלת על שאינו גופה יותר מגופה, שהרי שנינו: חותך מן העובר שבמעיה מותר באכילה, מן הטחול ומן הכליות אסור באכילה (= p_harbe_matzelet; again at 73a.14)

supports.gloss_en: שהרי שנינו: חותך מן העובר שבמעיה מותר באכילה, מן הטחול ומן הכליות אסור באכילה -- the mother's slaughter permits the fetus's pieces but not her own organs' (no SupportKind names a mishna citation)
תניא נמי הכי -- baraita B carries the Sages' טרפה תוכיח that Rava restores
דרבה בר בר חנה קאי כוותיה -- R' Yochanan (via Rabba bar bar Chana) reads the baraita's prohibition of the slaughtered hanging limb as only a mitzva of separation, so slaughter does not make it fallen
מנא הא מלתא דאמור רבנן... דכתיב במתם יטמא -- Rava's scriptural source for the received rule (no SupportKind names a derivation)

frames.gloss_en: במאי עסקינן? -- which limb is R' Yochanan's 'all agree' about?

alternatives.gloss_en: eliminated: on the fetus's limb they dispute
the survivor: an animal's hanging limb (then met by מיתה תנינא, שחיטה תנינא)

frames.gloss_en: Rava: למעוטי מאי? -- what does 'in their death' exclude?

alternatives.gloss_en: eliminated: impurity in their life is already excluded by 'their carcass'
the survivor: שמע מינה -- death makes fallen and slaughter does not

objections.gloss_en: מאי קאמר? -- 'it protects what is not her body more' does not answer 'if so, let it permit it for eating'

answered_by.gloss_en: חסורי מחסרא והכי קתני -- the baraita is lacking the Sages' טרפה תוכיח and R' Meir's reply (= p_rava_chasurei_mechasra)

objections.gloss_en: אם כן תתירנו באכילה! -- if the mother's slaughter purifies the limb, it should also permit it for eating

answered_by.gloss_en: טרפה תוכיח -- the tereifa's slaughter purifies it and does not permit it for eating (= p_tereifa_shechita_metaheret_velo_matira; the binyan_av m_tereifa_tochiach_73a)

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: R' Meir in the baraita grants that slaughter purifies the hanging limb -- yet by Reish Lakish he disputes it

answered_by.gloss_en: בשלמא לרבי שמעון בן לקיש -- לדבריהם קאמר להו: לדידי לא שנא אבר דעובר ולא שנא אבר דבהמה, כי הדדי נינהו -- he argued on the Sages' terms

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: R' Meir in the baraita grants that slaughter purifies the hanging limb -- yet by R' Yochanan all agree slaughter makes it fallen. אלא לרבי יוחנן קשיא (73b.2)
והא הוכשרו קתני! -- the mishna says 'they' were made susceptible, plural, so not the flesh alone

answered_by.gloss_en: מהו דתימא: חד לבשר הפורש מן הבהמה, וחד לבשר הפורש מן האבר (= p_trei_basar)

objections.gloss_en: ומאי אולמיה דהאי מהאי? -- why would the one kind of flesh need stating more than the other?

answered_by.gloss_en: סלקא דעתך אמינא: הואיל ומטמא טומאה חמורה אגב אביו, אימא לא ליבעי הכשר -- קמשמע לן

objections.gloss_en: לא תציתו ליה -- Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta reports in Rav's name: not flogged

answered_by.gloss_en: Rav Huna: אנן אמאן נסמוך? Rav Yosef: מאי קושיא? כי אמרי אנא במיתה דעושה ניפול, כי אמר איהו בשחיטה דאינה עושה ניפול (= p_lokeh_bemita, p_eino_lokeh_bishchita)

objections.gloss_en: והא קרא בשרצים כתיב! -- the verse is written of creeping things

answered_by.gloss_en: אם אינו ענין לשרצים, דלאו בני שחיטה נינהו -- תנהו ענין לבהמה

objections.gloss_en: ואכתי מיבעי ליה, כעין מיתה: לחין מטמאים, יבשים אין מטמאים! -- 'in their death' is still needed for 'like at death': moist impart impurity, dry do not

answered_by.gloss_en: תרי במותם כתיבי -- 'in their death' is written twice (Lev 11:31, 11:32)
